claims.text: Gas-atomized FeCoNiCrAl powder with a 15–45 μm particle-size range is optimal feedstock for producing high-quality coatings.
The baseline HVAF-i7 process using 15–45 μm feedstock produces acceptable-quality FeCoNiCrAl coatings but insufficient thickness.
A nozzle distance of approximately 300–350 mm is an optimal range for FeCoNiCrAl deposition with the HVAF-i7 torch.
Reducing the nozzle distance to 300–350 mm will increase in-flight particle velocity.
The increased particle velocity will increase particle kinetic energy at impact.
Greater impact kinetic energy will improve splat flattening and inter-particle cohesion.
Improved splat formation and inter-particle cohesion will increase deposition efficiency and coating thickness.
The higher impact velocity will promote better coating adhesion.
A shorter in-flight exposure resulting from the reduced nozzle distance will maintain low oxidation levels.
The proposed HVAF-i7 adjustment reproduces beneficial deposition behavior observed for MCrAlY bond coats after spray-distance optimization.
Relative to the longer-distance HVAF-i7 baseline, the reduced nozzle distance will produce a significantly thicker FeCoNiCrAl bond coat.
The thicker coating will retain acceptable adhesion and mechanical integrity.
The reduced-distance coating will have oxidation levels comparable to those of the baseline coating.
The reduced-distance coating will retain an acceptable microstructure while exhibiting improved deposition efficiency.
FeCoNiCrAl-family coatings can exhibit useful elevated-temperature oxidation-related performance.
The intervention will remain effective during high-temperature thermal-barrier service.
The intervention will remain effective for deposition inside components with internal diameters as small as 120 mm.
Excessive particle overheating or in-flight oxidation caused by nozzle-distance adjustment could limit the intervention's efficacy.
The exact thickness improvement and subtle changes in microstructure or oxidation kinetics are uncertain and require experimental validation.
